title: Per-room exception containment — does the vendored colyseus skill prevent 0.17/0.18 drift?

pinned.note: The skill documents 0.18. Its own Step 1 tells the reader to follow the pinned version's docs instead. Everything under `drift` is a shape that only 0.18 recall produces.

traps.why: 0.18 turned the Room generic into an options object, Room<{ state, metadata, client }>. On 0.15 the generic is the state class and this does not type-check.
0.17 client API. The 0.15 client listens through room.state.onChange and .listen; getStateCallbacks does not exist.
0.18 renamed the browser client package. This repository is on colyseus.js.
0.18 passes a close code as onLeave's second argument. The installed 0.15 signature is onLeave(client, consented?: boolean), so a close-code reading inverts the consented branch.
Harmless on 0.15, which shallow-merges anyway. It is only written by someone working around 0.18's wholesale replace, so it is evidence of 0.18 recall rather than a fault.
The 0.15 form, correct as it stands. An arm that 'migrates' it to a bare `extends Room` with a state field assignment has applied 0.18 to a 0.15 room.

CLAUDE.md: import from @colyseus/core. The meta-package re-exports via __exportStar, which Node's static CJS export detection cannot see, so this compiles and fails at runtime under the unbundled dev server. Present in both arms, so it measures the house rule rather than the skill.
CLAUDE.md: backend and frontend relative imports carry the real .ts extension; only shared uses .js. A copied import line is the documented way this breaks.
Issue 627 says ending the room by announcing anything is a twelfth SERVER_MSG and a design change, and recommends ending without an announcement. A new name here means the arm widened the task.
Acceptance criterion 1. Colyseus gates its whole wrapping mechanism on this hook merely existing.
Acceptance criterion 6. MatchRoom is the server half of the wire contract and nothing imports it today.
